task_3.title: Auto-create temporary indexes for 1D unindexed .sel() coordinates
task_3.description: xarray label-based selection now works on one-dimensional coordinates that are present in coords but do not have an explicit index by creating a temporary PandasIndex for the selection call. Multi-dimensional coordinates still require an explicit set_xindex() and invalid selection names continue to fail.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `Dataset.sel()` and `DataArray.sel()` support label-based selection on eligible one-dimensional coordinates even when the user has not explicitly created an index for that coordinate first.

expectation.grounded: `xarray.Dataset.sel()` and `xarray.DataArray.sel()` should accept indexers for coordinate names found in `.coords` but absent from `.xindexes` when that coordinate is one-dimensional, by creating a temporary `xarray.indexes.PandasIndex` for the lookup. This should cover both dimension coordinates whose index is missing and auxiliary one-dimensional coordinates aligned to a dimension. If the requested coordinate exists in `.coords` but has more than one dimension, automatic index creation should not occur and the operation should raise `ValueError`, with explicit `set_xindex()` remaining the required path. Names that are neither valid dimensions nor coordinates should continue to raise `KeyError`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to select by label on any supported one-dimensional coordinate without pre-registering an index. The library should transparently perform that lookup for the current selection only, while still rejecting unsupported coordinate shapes and invalid selection names with the appropriate error types.

constraints.grounded: The auto-created `PandasIndex` must be ephemeral for the selection call and must not register a persistent new entry in `.xindexes`. Existing `.sel()` behavior for coordinates that already have indexes must remain unchanged, and validation for invalid dimension or coordinate names must continue to raise `KeyError`.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade should add convenience for eligible one-dimensional coordinates without silently changing stored index state, altering established indexed-selection behavior, or relaxing validation for unsupported selection targets.

behavior: When `.sel()` targets a coordinate that exists in `.coords`, has no explicit xindex, and is one-dimensional, the selection is performed using a temporary `PandasIndex` instead of failing because the coordinate is unindexed.
The automatic lookup applies to both `Dataset.sel()` and `DataArray.sel()` because label-based selection now synthesizes an index for eligible coordinates during index grouping.
Automatic index creation is limited to one-dimensional coordinates; selecting against a coordinate with more than one dimension raises `ValueError` rather than auto-indexing it.
Selection requests for names that are not dimensions or coordinates still raise `KeyError`.
Successful selection on an unindexed one-dimensional coordinate does not persist a new explicit index on the original object.
acceptance_criteria: Given a `Dataset` or `DataArray` with a one-dimensional coordinate in `coords` but no explicit index for that coordinate, when `.sel()` is called with that coordinate name and a matching label, then the selection should succeed and return the same subset a corresponding explicit index would have produced.

Given an auxiliary one-dimensional coordinate attached to an existing dimension, when `.sel()` is called with that coordinate name, then label-based selection should work without requiring a prior `set_xindex()` call.
Given a coordinate present in `coords` with more than one dimension, when `.sel()` targets that coordinate, then the operation should raise `ValueError` instead of auto-creating an index for it.
Given a selection name that is neither a valid dimension nor a coordinate, when `.sel()` is called, then the operation should continue to raise `KeyError`.

Given a successful `.sel()` on an unindexed one-dimensional coordinate, when the original object is inspected afterward, then it should still not have gained a persistent explicit index as a side effect.

task_2.title: Automatic xindex replacement on reindexing
task_2.description: Xarray 2026.1.0 changes `Dataset.set_xindex()` and `DataArray.set_xindex()` so that setting an index on coordinates that are already indexed replaces the prior index instead of failing. Consumers should rely on direct index replacement behavior and no longer require a separate `drop_indexes()` step, while preserving existing validation for invalid targets.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that calling `Dataset.set_xindex()` or `DataArray.set_xindex()` on coordinates that already have an index replaces that index in a single call instead of failing or requiring a prior `drop_indexes()` call.

expectation.grounded: `xarray.Dataset.set_xindex()` and `xarray.DataArray.set_xindex()` should accept target coordinate names even when those coordinates are already present in `.xindexes`, construct the requested Xarray-compatible index from the provided coordinates, and return an object with the existing index replaced by the new index. The call should no longer raise `ValueError` solely because the target coordinate already has an index.
expectation.conceptual: Reapplying `set_xindex()` to an already indexed coordinate should behave as a direct replacement operation from the caller's perspective: the API should succeed, update the coordinate's index to the requested one, and eliminate the need for a manual index-removal step beforehand.

constraints.grounded: This change only removes the conflict for coordinates that already have an index. Existing validation around valid coordinate targets, index construction, and other error conditions should remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should make index replacement easier without broadening what counts as a valid `set_xindex()` call or weakening other existing safeguards.

behavior: `Dataset.set_xindex()` should no longer fail just because one or more requested coordinates already have an index.
`DataArray.set_xindex()` should expose the same replacement behavior for already indexed coordinates.
When an index is set again for the same coordinate, the returned object should reflect the newly requested index rather than preserving the old one.
Users should be able to replace an existing index through `set_xindex()` directly, without first calling `drop_indexes()`.
acceptance_criteria: When `Dataset.set_xindex()` is called for a coordinate that already has an index, it should succeed and the returned dataset should expose the replacement index for that coordinate.
When `DataArray.set_xindex()` is called for a coordinate that already has an index, it should succeed and the returned data array should expose the replacement index for that coordinate.
When callers repeat `set_xindex()` on the same coordinate, they should not need to remove the existing index beforehand.
When `set_xindex()` is called with other invalid inputs, it should continue to fail according to the API's existing validation rules.

task_1.title: Improve DataTree HTML display for large trees
task_1.description: The upgrade changes xarray's `DataTree` HTML representation to make notebook and docs output easier to navigate. Child groups are individually collapsible and show subtree item counts, index information is included in HTML output, and large trees are automatically collapsed or truncated using configurable display limits instead of trying to fully render everything.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the `DataTree` HTML representation stays informative and usable as tree size grows: groups should be individually collapsible, show how much content they contain, expose index information in HTML output, and automatically collapse or truncate oversized trees according to configured display limits.

expectation.grounded: `xarray.DataTree` HTML repr should render each child group as its own collapsible section label instead of using a separate collapsible `Groups` section. Group labels should include a subtree item count. The HTML repr should include an `Indexes` section when indexes are eligible for display, following the existing `display_default_indexes` filtering behavior. Large trees should respect `display_max_children`, `display_max_items`, and `display_max_html_elements`: `display_max_children` limits how many child groups are shown per node, `display_max_items` controls when additional groups start collapsed, and `display_max_html_elements` caps rendered HTML detail and replaces excess node detail with a truncated placeholder. The public display defaults should reflect `display_max_children=12`, `display_max_items=20`, and `display_max_html_elements=300`.
expectation.conceptual: The HTML preview for `DataTree` should expose the same important structure users can inspect in other representations, while remaining readable for large trees. Users should be able to expand individual groups, see how much content a group contains, inspect indexes in HTML output, and avoid overwhelming notebook output because large trees collapse or truncate automatically based on display settings.

constraints.grounded: This upgrade should affect HTML display behavior only. Existing section types such as dimensions, coordinates, data variables, inherited coordinates at the root, indexes, and attributes should remain organized as observable sections within each node. Trees that do not exceed the configured limits should render without truncation, and limit-driven collapsing or truncation must be controlled by the display options rather than by data mutation or by removing interactive expansion from nodes that are still renderable.
constraints.conceptual: The change must preserve the meaning of the displayed tree and only improve how it is presented. Small trees should still render fully, while large trees should degrade gracefully through collapsing and truncation rather than by hiding important structure entirely or changing the underlying data.

behavior: Each visible `DataTree` group becomes independently collapsible in the HTML repr.
Every group label shows a parenthesized count of the items contained in that group's subtree.
The HTML repr now surfaces an `Indexes` section when applicable, aligning HTML output more closely with the text representation.
`display_max_children` limits the number of child groups shown for any node by keeping leading and trailing groups visible and replacing omitted middle groups with an omission indicator.
`display_max_items` determines when additional groups in a large tree should default to collapsed instead of expanded.
`display_max_html_elements` limits how much detailed HTML is rendered; once exceeded, further node detail is replaced by a truncated placeholder rather than being fully emitted.
When auto-collapse is triggered within a sibling group set, the immediate sibling groups should start collapsed consistently at that level.
acceptance_criteria: When a `DataTree` is rendered as HTML, each child group should have its own expandable label and that label should include an item count.
When a rendered `DataTree` has displayable indexes, the HTML output should include an `Indexes` section in addition to the other node sections.

When a node has more children than allowed by `display_max_children`, the HTML output should show only the configured leading and trailing child groups with an omission marker for the hidden middle portion.
When the overall displayed tree content exceeds `display_max_items`, later groups should remain present but start collapsed instead of expanding all details by default.
When rendering the full detail would exceed `display_max_html_elements`, the HTML repr should stop emitting full node detail beyond the limit and show a truncated placeholder for the affected nodes.
When a tree remains within the configured limits, the HTML repr should render the available node sections without truncation.

task_4.title: Require h5netcdf 1.4+ for complex data compatibility
task_4.description: Raise the minimum supported h5netcdf version to 1.4 so the h5netcdf backend can rely on the backend's newer complex-number storage behavior, which is aligned with NetCDF4/libnetcdf4 semantics, instead of supporting older compatibility behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the h5netcdf backend only supports h5netcdf 1.4 or newer, and that users who persist complex-valued data through that backend get the backend behavior introduced in h5netcdf 1.4, aligned with NetCDF4-style storage semantics.

expectation.grounded: The library should require `h5netcdf>=1.4` for use of the `h5netcdf` backend. For datasets containing complex-valued variables, behavior when writing and reading through the `h5netcdf` engine should follow the improved complex-number storage semantics provided by h5netcdf 1.4, with alignment to `libnetcdf4`/NetCDF4 behavior rather than older backend-specific compatibility handling.
expectation.conceptual: Users of the h5netcdf backend should need a modern supported h5netcdf version, and complex-valued data saved with that backend should behave consistently with the standard NetCDF4 experience instead of depending on legacy compatibility modes.

constraints.grounded: Do not preserve support expectations for `h5netcdf` versions below 1.4. Do not introduce a separate user-facing API contract for legacy complex-number handling; the supported contract should be the native behavior of `h5netcdf>=1.4` as used through the existing `h5netcdf` backend.
constraints.conceptual: Older unsupported backend versions should no longer be treated as valid targets, and the upgrade should not create a second, special behavior path for complex data on supported versions.

behavior: The supported version floor for the h5netcdf backend is raised to h5netcdf 1.4.
Complex-valued datasets handled through the h5netcdf backend are expected to use the complex-number storage behavior available in h5netcdf 1.4 and later.
The supported h5netcdf backend contract for complex data is aligned with NetCDF4/libnetcdf4 semantics rather than pre-1.4 compatibility behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a user selects or installs support for the h5netcdf backend, the supported h5netcdf version range should begin at 1.4.

When a dataset containing complex-valued variables is written and then reopened through the h5netcdf backend on a supported h5netcdf version, it should follow the backend behavior aligned with the NetCDF4 experience.
When a user remains on h5netcdf versions older than 1.4, that environment should be considered unsupported for the h5netcdf backend rather than partially compatible.

task_5.title: Configurable coordinate compatibility for arithmetic
task_5.description: Adds a new `arithmetic_compat` option to `xarray.set_options()` so users can control how binary arithmetic handles same-named non-index coordinates that may conflict. The default remains `minimal`, preserving prior behavior, and the same compatibility choice is exposed for direct coordinate merging.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can choose how binary arithmetic resolves same-named non-index coordinates, including strict validation, conflict-tolerant merging, first-operand override, and the existing default behavior of dropping conflicting coordinates.

expectation.grounded: `xarray.set_options()` must accept an `arithmetic_compat` option with the values `identical`, `equals`, `broadcast_equals`, `no_conflicts`, `override`, and `minimal`. `DataArray` and `Dataset` binary operations must use this setting when merging non-index coordinates of the same name: `identical` requires matching values, dimensions, and attributes; `equals` requires matching values and dimensions; `broadcast_equals` requires equality after broadcasting; `no_conflicts` requires agreement where both sides are non-null and combines non-null values; `override` skips comparison and keeps the first operand's coordinate; and `minimal` drops conflicting coordinates. Incompatible comparisons must surface as `MergeError`. `Coordinates.merge()` must also accept a `compat` keyword with the same choices and default to `minimal`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to decide whether arithmetic between xarray objects strictly validates non-index coordinates, merges them when they do not conflict, keeps the left operand's coordinate without checking, or removes conflicting coordinates. The same compatibility choice should also be available when coordinate collections are merged directly.

constraints.grounded: The new compatibility setting applies only to non-index coordinates with matching names during coordinate merge steps in arithmetic; index alignment remains controlled by `arithmetic_join`. The default must remain `arithmetic_compat='minimal'`, matching pre-upgrade behavior when users do not opt into another mode. Values outside the supported compatibility options must not be accepted.
constraints.conceptual: This feature must not change ordinary arithmetic alignment rules or force behavior changes on existing users. If no new option is chosen, arithmetic should continue to behave as it did before for coordinate conflicts.

behavior: `xr.set_options()` exposes a new `arithmetic_compat` setting for arithmetic-time handling of same-named non-index coordinates.
Binary operations on `DataArray` use `arithmetic_compat` when merging coordinate metadata from both operands.
Binary operations on `Dataset` use `arithmetic_compat` when merging coordinate metadata from both operands.
In-place `DataArray` arithmetic applies the same compatibility policy when deciding whether coordinate metadata can be merged or must fail.
`Coordinates.merge()` accepts a `compat` argument so direct coordinate merges can use the same conflict policy outside binary arithmetic.
The default `minimal` mode preserves existing behavior by dropping conflicting non-index coordinates instead of changing alignment or comparison defaults.
acceptance_criteria: When `xr.set_options(arithmetic_compat='minimal')` is active and two operands carry conflicting non-index coordinates with the same name, the arithmetic result should omit that conflicting non-index coordinate while still producing the arithmetic data result.

When `xr.set_options(arithmetic_compat='override')` is active, arithmetic should keep the first operand's non-index coordinate for the conflicting name without comparing it, so reversing operand order may change which coordinate is retained.

When `xr.set_options(arithmetic_compat='no_conflicts')` is active and overlapping non-null coordinate values do not disagree, arithmetic should return a merged non-index coordinate containing the combined non-null values.

When a strict comparison mode such as `identical`, `equals`, or `broadcast_equals` is active and same-named non-index coordinates are incompatible under that rule, the arithmetic operation should raise `MergeError`.
When no `arithmetic_compat` override is supplied, binary arithmetic should continue to use `minimal` behavior by default.
When `Coordinates.merge(..., compat=...)` is called, the coordinate merge result should honor the selected compatibility mode independently of the global arithmetic option.

task_6.title: Improve xarray coordinate display ordering
task_6.description: xarray 2026.1.0 changes the visible ordering of coordinates when DataArray and Dataset objects are displayed. Coordinate listings now follow dimension order more intuitively by grouping auxiliary coordinates with their related dimensions and leaving scalar or unrelated coordinates at the end, consistently across text and HTML displays.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that coordinates shown when displaying xarray objects are ordered by the object's dimensions so that each dimension coordinate appears before related auxiliary coordinates, producing a more intuitive and consistent representation.

expectation.grounded: When xarray objects such as DataArray, Dataset, or coordinate views are rendered through repr() or HTML display, coordinate entries should be sorted by the object's dimension tuple. For each dimension section, the dimension coordinate whose name matches that dimension should appear first, followed by non-dimension coordinates associated with that dimension. A coordinate that spans multiple dimensions should be placed with the section for its last matching dimension. Scalar coordinates, or coordinates whose dimensions are not present in the object's dimensions, should be listed after all dimension-associated coordinate groups.
expectation.conceptual: Displayed coordinate lists should read in the same order as the object's dimensions, with primary dimension labels first, related helper coordinates shown beside the dimensions they describe, and scalar or unrelated metadata left to the end.

constraints.grounded: This upgrade must not change stored coordinate values, dimension order, indexes, or computational behavior. The only intended change is the ordering of displayed coordinate sections, and the same ordering contract should apply in both plain-text and HTML representations.
constraints.conceptual: Treat this as a presentation-only change. It should make displays easier to read without changing the object's data model or causing different display surfaces to disagree about coordinate order.

behavior: Coordinate sections in xarray displays are ordered by the parent object's dimension order rather than only by insertion or a flat dimension-first split.
Within each dimension group, the dimension coordinate itself is shown before auxiliary coordinates tied to that dimension.
One-dimensional auxiliary coordinates are displayed immediately after the dimension they belong to, even when later dimensions also exist.
Auxiliary coordinates spanning multiple dimensions are grouped after the section for their last matching dimension so they do not interrupt earlier dimension groups.
Scalar coordinates and coordinates whose dimensions do not belong to the displayed object's dimensions remain at the end of the coordinate listing.
The same coordinate ordering is used in both text repr output and HTML notebook-style displays.
acceptance_criteria: When a displayed xarray object has dimension coordinates and auxiliary coordinates for each dimension, it should show each dimension coordinate first and then the auxiliary coordinates associated with that dimension before moving to the next dimension.

When an object has an auxiliary coordinate attached only to an earlier dimension and another dimension coordinate appears later in the dimension tuple, the earlier auxiliary coordinate should appear before that later dimension coordinate.
When an auxiliary coordinate spans multiple dimensions, it should appear after the section for the last matching dimension rather than between earlier dimension groups.
When scalar coordinates are present, they should be listed after all coordinates that are associated with the object's declared dimensions.
When the same object is viewed through plain-text repr and HTML display, the coordinate ordering should match.

task_7.title: Use StringDType for Zarr string reads
task_7.description: The upgrade changes runtime handling of Zarr string data: UTF-8 variable-length string variables are read back as native NumPy string dtypes when supported, including Zarr v3 serializer-based strings, and null detection for StringDType-backed arrays now follows the dtype's configured missing-value sentinel.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that reading Zarr string variables preserves them as native variable-length string data and that null-detection APIs treat StringDType-backed arrays according to the string dtype's configured missing-value sentinel.

expectation.grounded: When the library reads Zarr variables encoded as UTF-8 variable-length strings, including Zarr v3 arrays whose serializer identifies `vlen-utf8`, the resulting array dtype should be the library's variable-length string dtype rather than a fixed-width Unicode fallback. Null detection for arrays backed by `np.dtypes.StringDType` must use the dtype's `na_object`: NA-like sentinels should be reported as missing, while non-NA sentinels such as the default empty string should only mark matching elements as missing.
expectation.conceptual: Opening Zarr datasets with string variables should preserve those variables as native string arrays, and calling null-detection APIs on those arrays should report missing values based on the string dtype's configured sentinel.

constraints.grounded: Existing variable-length string detection for previously supported Zarr string encodings must continue to work. Missing-value behavior for non-string dtypes must remain unchanged. StringDType arrays whose configured sentinel is not NA-like must not treat unrelated values as missing.
constraints.conceptual: Do not regress existing Zarr string decoding or alter null semantics for non-string data, and avoid introducing false missing values for ordinary string content.

behavior: Zarr UTF-8 variable-length string variables are recognized as string data when read, including Zarr v3 arrays that advertise the `vlen-utf8` serializer.
String-valued Zarr data is surfaced with a variable-length string dtype instead of degrading to a fixed-width Unicode dtype when native string dtype support is available.
Null detection on `np.dtypes.StringDType` arrays consults the dtype's configured `na_object` rather than using generic floating-point null detection.
If a `StringDType` uses an NA-like sentinel such as `None` or `np.nan`, elements carrying that sentinel are reported as missing.
If a `StringDType` uses a non-NA sentinel such as the default empty string, only elements equal to that sentinel are reported as missing.
acceptance_criteria: When a Zarr variable stores UTF-8 variable-length strings, opening it through the library should expose the data as string-typed values rather than as a fixed-width Unicode fallback.
When the same string encoding is represented through Zarr v3 serializer metadata, the variable should still be decoded as string data on read.

When null-detection APIs are applied to a `np.dtypes.StringDType` array configured with `na_object=None` or `na_object=np.nan`, elements carrying that configured sentinel should be reported as missing.
When null-detection APIs are applied to a `np.dtypes.StringDType` array whose configured sentinel is the empty string, only empty-string entries should be reported as missing.

task_9.title: Include indexes in identical comparisons
task_9.description: The upgrade tightens xarray identity checks so indexes are now part of object identity for Dataset, DataArray, and assert_identical comparisons. Objects with matching data, coordinates, and attributes are no longer treated as identical when their indexed coordinates differ, their index types differ, or their indexes are unequal, and assertion failures now surface index differences.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset.identical(), DataArray.identical(), and xarray.testing.assert_identical() treat indexes as part of identity, so objects are only considered identical when their indexed coordinate definitions and index semantics match in addition to their existing data, coordinate, name, and attribute checks.

expectation.grounded: For Dataset.identical() and DataArray.identical(), identity must include xindexes: both objects must expose the same indexed coordinate names, the corresponding indexes must be the same concrete index type, and each matching pair must compare equal via Index.equals(). If a custom Index does not implement equality and raises NotImplementedError, identity should fall back to comparing the indexed coordinate variables for that coordinate. xarray.testing.assert_identical() must fail with AssertionError when indexes exist only on one side or when matching coordinates have non-identical indexes, and its diff output should report index-only differences as part of the assertion diagnostics.
expectation.conceptual: Identity checks should now include whether coordinates are indexed and what those indexes mean, not just the raw data and metadata. Two objects that look the same by values should still be treated as different if their index attachment, index type, or index equality semantics differ, and comparison failures should clearly expose that the mismatch is in indexes.

constraints.grounded: This stricter behavior applies to the identical-family APIs and must not broaden the semantics of equals-style comparisons. Different index types for the same coordinate must be considered non-identical even when coordinate values match. When both sides have no indexes, identical behavior should remain unchanged. Custom indexes without a working equality implementation must still be comparable through their coordinate variables rather than failing solely because direct index equality is unavailable.
constraints.conceptual: Only identity checks become stricter; ordinary equality behavior should remain as before. The change should reject structurally different indexing, preserve existing outcomes when no indexes are involved, and still allow semantically equivalent custom indexes to compare as identical when their coordinate definitions match.

behavior: Dataset.identical() now returns false when two datasets differ in which coordinates have xindexes, even if their data, coordinates, and attributes otherwise match.
DataArray.identical() now returns false when two arrays carry different xindexes for the same coordinates, including cases where one side has an extra index.
For identical comparisons, matching indexed coordinates must use the same index class; differing index types make the objects non-identical even if coordinate values are the same.
When index objects support Index.equals(), that result determines whether matching indexes are identical.
When direct index equality is unavailable and raises NotImplementedError, identical comparisons fall back to comparing the indexed coordinate variables for that coordinate.
xarray.testing.assert_identical() now raises AssertionError for index mismatches and includes index-specific diagnostics, such as indexes present on only one side or differing index representations.
acceptance_criteria: When two Dataset objects differ only because one has an additional xindex on a coordinate, Dataset.identical() should return false and xarray.testing.assert_identical() should fail.
When two DataArray objects have the same data and coordinates but different xindex membership for a coordinate, they should not be considered identical.
When two objects index the same coordinate with different index types, identical comparison should report them as non-identical even if the coordinate values match.
When two objects have the same indexed coordinate names, the same index types, and equal indexes, identical comparison should continue to succeed.

When a custom index cannot perform direct equality but the corresponding indexed coordinate variables are equal, identical comparison should still succeed instead of failing only because direct index equality is unavailable.
When assert_identical fails because of index differences, the failure should expose the mismatch as an index-related difference rather than only as a generic data or coordinate mismatch.

task_8.title: Align open_zarr auto chunking with the Zarr engine
task_8.description: The upgrade changes `xarray.open_zarr()` so that omitting `chunks` preserves the prior default behavior, while explicitly passing `chunks="auto"` now performs the same automatic chunking as `xarray.open_dataset(..., engine="zarr")`. This removes the previous special case where `"auto"` behaved like the default loading path instead of true auto chunking.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `xarray.open_zarr()` treats an omitted `chunks` argument differently from an explicit `chunks="auto"`, so that explicit auto chunking is consistent with `xarray.open_dataset(..., engine="zarr")` while the existing default behavior remains unchanged when `chunks` is not provided.

expectation.grounded: `xarray.open_zarr()` should use its existing default loading behavior only when `chunks` is omitted: use `chunks={}` when a chunk manager such as dask is available, otherwise `chunks=None`. When callers explicitly pass `chunks="auto"`, `open_zarr()` should no longer remap that value to the default path, and should instead apply the same auto-chunking semantics as `xarray.open_dataset(..., engine="zarr", chunks="auto")`.
expectation.conceptual: Users who explicitly request automatic chunking when opening a Zarr store should get true auto-chunking behavior that matches the generic dataset-opening API, while callers who leave chunking unspecified should continue to see the same default behavior they had before the upgrade.

constraints.grounded: Do not change observable behavior for `open_zarr()` calls that omit `chunks`. Preserve support for the documented `chunks` inputs, and keep explicit `chunks="auto"` distinct from the omitted/default case rather than treating it as equivalent to `chunks={}` or `chunks=None`.
constraints.conceptual: Only the meaning of explicitly requesting auto chunking should change. Existing callers that rely on the default chunk-loading behavior without specifying `chunks` should not see a regression.

behavior: Calling `xarray.open_zarr()` without a `chunks` argument continues to follow the previous default loading path instead of changing to true auto chunking.
Calling `xarray.open_zarr(..., chunks="auto")` now preserves the explicit auto-chunking request instead of converting it into the default chunk-loading behavior.
For Zarr inputs, `xarray.open_zarr(..., chunks="auto")` now matches `xarray.open_dataset(..., engine="zarr", chunks="auto")` in how it determines dataset chunking.

Because explicit auto chunking is now honored, the returned dataset's chunk layout may differ from the store's native Zarr chunk layout and may differ from the chunk layout produced by omitting `chunks`.
acceptance_criteria: When `xarray.open_zarr()` is called without `chunks`, it should preserve the same observable chunk-loading behavior as before the upgrade.
When `xarray.open_zarr(..., chunks="auto")` is used, it should no longer behave the same as leaving `chunks` unset.

When the same Zarr store is opened with `xarray.open_zarr(..., chunks="auto")` and `xarray.open_dataset(..., engine="zarr", chunks="auto")`, both calls should expose equivalent auto-chunking behavior.

When a Zarr store's native chunking differs from the library's auto-chunking choice, explicit `chunks="auto"` should return the auto-chunked layout rather than silently falling back to the default loading behavior.

task_12.title: Preserve datetime units in seasonal resampling
task_12.description: The 2026.1.0 update fixes seasonal resampling so `SeasonResampler` keeps the original `datetime64` unit of pandas-backed time coordinates instead of silently converting output labels to a different resolution. This aligns seasonal resampling with other xarray resampling behavior and prevents downstream dtype changes caused by the resample output.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that seasonal resampling with `SeasonResampler` preserves the original datetime resolution of pandas-backed time coordinates instead of changing the output coordinate dtype during resample operations.

expectation.grounded: When `xarray.groupers.SeasonResampler` is used through `.resample(time=...)` on data backed by a `pandas.DatetimeIndex`, the resulting `time` coordinate should retain the input index's `datetime64` unit. Output seasonal labels emitted by the resample operation should remain in the same datetime unit as the source time coordinate. Existing `CFTimeIndex` seasonal resampling behavior should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Season-based resampling should behave like other xarray resampling operations: the output time labels must keep the same datetime precision as the input instead of being silently promoted to a different resolution. Non-NumPy calendar handling should continue to work as before.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the public `SeasonResampler` API, season grouping semantics, or the calendar type returned for cftime-backed coordinates. Preserve the observable seasonal labels and aggregated results while correcting datetime unit preservation for pandas-backed datetime coordinates.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should not change how seasons are defined, ordered, or reduced. It should only remove the unintended datetime precision change in the resampled coordinate and avoid regressions for alternate calendar inputs.

behavior: `SeasonResampler` now preserves the original `datetime64` unit from a pandas-backed `time` index in resampled outputs.
Seasonal coordinate labels generated by the resample operation use the same datetime resolution as the source `time` coordinate rather than defaulting to a finer unit.
Seasonal resampling remains compatible with cftime-backed coordinates and continues to return cftime-based output coordinates for those inputs.
acceptance_criteria: When data with a pandas-backed `time` coordinate using a specific `datetime64` unit is resampled with `SeasonResampler`, the resulting `time` coordinate should use that same unit.
When input data uses a non-default unit such as `datetime64[s]`, seasonal resampling should preserve that exact unit in the output coordinate instead of converting it to a finer resolution.
When `SeasonResampler` is applied to cftime-backed time coordinates, it should continue to return cftime-based output coordinates rather than converting them to pandas or NumPy datetimes.

task_11.title: Honor xindexes while tolerating sliced RangeIndex drift
task_11.description: The upgrade fixes equality and identity behavior for range-based xindexes with floating-point coordinates. Equivalent RangeIndex values produced through slicing should no longer compare as different because of tiny accumulated rounding differences, while strict exact comparison remains available for callers that need it.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that equality and identity checks do not treat equivalent floating-point RangeIndex xindexes as different solely because slicing introduced insignificant rounding drift, while preserving a strict mode for exact comparisons and continuing to reject genuinely different or differently typed indexes.

expectation.grounded: RangeIndex.equals() must support an exact keyword that defaults to non-exact comparison. In the default mode, two RangeIndex instances should compare equal when they are both RangeIndex, have the same size, and their floating-point bounds are equivalent within normal floating-point tolerance even if slicing changed the stored start or stop values slightly. With exact=True, RangeIndex.equals() must require exact equality of the stored bounds and size. RangeCoordinateTransform.equals() must follow the same exact-versus-tolerant behavior. Comparisons against non-RangeIndex index types must return False. The identical family must treat xindexes as part of identity, requiring matching xindex type and equality when an index-level equality method is available, otherwise comparing coordinates.
expectation.conceptual: Normal equality and identity checks should accept range-based floating-point indexes that represent the same coordinates, even if one was produced by slicing and carries tiny rounding differences internally. Users must be able to request strict comparison when exact stored values matter, and identity checks must continue to notice missing, differently typed, or meaningfully different indexes.

constraints.grounded: Do not relax comparison across different index classes. Do not ignore size mismatches or materially different range bounds. exact=True must preserve strict inequality for even very small floating-point differences. Identity checks that include xindexes must still fail when an xindex exists only on one side, has a different type, or is not equal by its own equality semantics.
constraints.conceptual: Only insignificant floating-point drift should be tolerated. Real differences in index type, presence, length, or values must still be surfaced, and strict comparison must remain available for callers that depend on exact internal state.

behavior: RangeCoordinateTransform.equals() now supports exact=False by default and treats floating-point start and stop values with tolerant comparison while still requiring equal size.
RangeCoordinateTransform.equals(exact=True) requires exact start, stop, and size equality.
RangeIndex.equals() is now explicitly implemented, accepts exact, and delegates equality to the underlying range transform.
RangeIndex.equals() returns False when the other object is not a RangeIndex.
Equivalent RangeIndex objects created through direct construction versus slicing can compare equal by default even when floating-point accumulation changes stored bounds slightly.
Identity-style comparisons now treat xindexes as part of object identity instead of ignoring them.
acceptance_criteria: When two floating-point RangeIndex objects represent the same coordinate sequence but one was derived by slicing and has minor rounding drift in its stored bounds, calling equals() without exact=True should report them as equal.
When the same two RangeIndex objects are compared with exact=True, the comparison should report them as unequal if their stored floating-point bounds are not exactly the same.
When two RangeIndex objects differ in size, start, or stop by a meaningful amount, equals() should report them as unequal.
When a RangeIndex is compared with a different index type, equals() should report them as unequal.
When identity-style comparison is performed on objects that carry xindexes, equivalent xindexes should be included in the identity decision rather than ignored.
When two objects differ only by xindex presence, xindex type, or non-equal xindex values, identity-style comparison should not consider them identical.

task_10.title: Normalize keep_attrs behavior for single-input apply_ufunc and where
task_10.description: This update fixes inconsistent attribute propagation in xarray operations backed by apply_ufunc, especially xr.where when only one xarray object participates. Coordinate metadata now follows the requested keep_attrs policy consistently so preserved metadata stays available when requested and is removed when dropping attrs is requested.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray operations built on apply_ufunc handle coordinate and result attrs consistently when only one xarray object is involved, so keep_attrs preserve modes retain metadata and drop modes remove it instead of leaking attrs from the lone xarray input.

expectation.grounded: In xarray.apply_ufunc(), the drop-attrs modes (keep_attrs=False and keep_attrs='drop') must clear attrs from output coordinates even when output coordinates are derived from exactly one xarray input. In xarray.where(), attr-preservation must be consistent across preserve and drop modes: keep_attrs=True and the override-style preservation path should preserve attrs on the resulting xarray structure, while keep_attrs=False should remove attrs, including coordinate attrs when cond is the only xarray argument and x/y are scalars or other non-xarray values.
expectation.conceptual: Attribute retention for apply_ufunc-based operations should no longer depend on how many xarray operands were provided. If callers choose to keep attrs, the returned object should consistently keep the relevant metadata; if callers choose to drop attrs, the returned object should not retain coordinate metadata from the only xarray input.

constraints.grounded: The change must only affect attr propagation semantics. Data values, dimensions, coordinate labels, index construction, and normal broadcasting/alignment behavior must remain unchanged. Existing multi-input attr handling should continue to honor the selected keep_attrs policy; only the single-input inconsistency should be removed.
constraints.conceptual: This fix should change metadata behavior only. It must not alter the computed data, shape, coordinates, or alignment rules of the affected operations, and it should preserve existing behavior outside the inconsistent single-input attr case.

behavior: When apply_ufunc builds output coordinates from a single xarray input under a drop-attrs policy, the output coordinate attrs are empty instead of being copied through from that input.
When xr.where is called with keep_attrs=False and only cond is an xarray object, the returned xarray object's coordinate attrs are dropped even if x and y are scalars.

When xr.where is called with keep_attrs=True, attrs are preserved consistently on the returned xarray structure rather than varying based on whether another xarray operand also contributes coordinates.
The override-style attr-preservation path in xr.where follows the same preservation behavior as explicit keep_attrs=True.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller runs xr.where(cond, scalar_x, scalar_y, keep_attrs=False) and cond carries coordinate attrs, the returned xarray object should expose the same coordinates without those attrs.
When a caller runs xr.where(cond, scalar_x, scalar_y, keep_attrs=True) and the xarray input carries coordinate attrs, the returned object should retain those coordinate attrs consistently.
When apply_ufunc is invoked in a mode that drops attrs and only one xarray object contributes coordinates, the output coordinates should not inherit attrs from that input.
When the preserve-attrs behavior is reached through the override-style keep_attrs mode, the observable attr retention should match the explicit preserve-attrs mode.

task_13.title: Fix pandas 3 string index compatibility
task_13.description: This update adds partial compatibility for pandas 3 default string indexes so xarray can create coordinates and indexes from string-valued pandas indexes in supported NumPy environments without failing during dtype conversion.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray operations can accept pandas 3 string-backed indexes as coordinate or dimension inputs without failing during dtype conversion, including when building a new dimension from a string-valued pandas index.

expectation.grounded: When `PandasIndexingAdapter` receives a `pd.StringDtype` and NumPy string dtypes are available, it should treat that dtype as `np.dtypes.StringDType` using the pandas dtype's configured missing-value object. Operations that create xarray variables from pandas indexes, including `xr.concat` with a string-valued `pd.Index` as `dim`, should no longer raise a dtype-interpretation `TypeError` solely because the index uses `pd.StringDtype`.
expectation.conceptual: String-valued pandas 3 indexes should behave as supported xarray inputs instead of crashing when xarray converts index data into coordinates or indexes.

constraints.grounded: Apply this compatibility handling only to pandas string extension dtypes in environments where NumPy string dtypes are supported. Preserve existing behavior for non-string dtypes and other already-supported pandas extension dtypes, and keep missing-value semantics aligned with the source pandas string dtype.
constraints.conceptual: The change should stay narrowly scoped to pandas 3 string index compatibility and should not alter how xarray handles unrelated index types or unsupported runtime environments.

behavior: `PandasIndexingAdapter` recognizes `pd.StringDtype` as a dedicated compatibility case when NumPy string dtypes are present.

Instead of relying on a generic NumPy dtype conversion that fails for pandas 3 string indexes, xarray uses a NumPy string dtype representation that remains compatible with the pandas string dtype's missing-value configuration.
User-facing operations that materialize coordinates or indexes from pandas 3 string indexes can complete without a dtype-conversion `TypeError` caused by `pd.StringDtype`.
acceptance_criteria: Given a pandas 3 string-valued `pd.Index` used as the `dim` argument to `xr.concat`, when xarray creates the new coordinate or index in an environment with NumPy string dtype support, the operation should succeed without raising a dtype-interpretation `TypeError` for `pd.StringDtype`.

When xarray exposes the dtype of a coordinate or index created from a pandas 3 string index in a supported environment, it should be represented as a NumPy string dtype rather than being rejected as an unsupported pandas extension dtype.
When the source pandas string dtype defines a missing-value object, xarray should preserve compatibility with that missing-value behavior in the resulting string dtype handling.

task_15.title: Restore where() compatibility for CuPy-backed arrays
task_15.description: The update fixes a runtime compatibility bug in xarray's where() handling for CuPy-backed data. Masking operations no longer fail when the selected array backend does not expose a namespace-level astype function, allowing where() to proceed using the backend array's own casting support while preserving existing masking semantics for other backends.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that where() works on xarray objects backed by cupy.array inputs instead of failing during dtype coercion when evaluating the condition.

expectation.grounded: Calls to where() on xarray objects backed by cupy.array inputs, including DataArray.where(...), should complete without raising AttributeError from backend dtype conversion. During where() evaluation, if the active array namespace does not provide a namespace-level astype function, xarray should use the input array object's own astype support so condition casting and value selection can proceed with the backend's native array behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Masking CuPy-backed xarray data should behave like masking on other supported array backends: the operation should run successfully, apply the mask, and return a normal result instead of failing because of backend-specific casting differences.

constraints.grounded: Do not change existing where() behavior for NumPy-backed inputs or for backends that already expose namespace-level astype. The fix should only remove the backend-specific casting failure and must not change where() fill-value handling, replacement-value semantics, or normal alignment and broadcasting behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve current masking behavior for already-working inputs. The change should only eliminate the backend compatibility failure, not alter how where() decides which values are kept or replaced.

behavior: where() no longer fails on cupy.array-backed inputs when converting the condition to the backend boolean dtype.
If the selected array namespace does not define a namespace-level astype function, xarray falls back to the array instance's astype method before continuing the where() operation.
Successful where() evaluation continues through the backend array namespace, so compatible non-NumPy arrays can complete masking without being blocked by missing namespace-level casting helpers.
acceptance_criteria: When a DataArray backed by cupy.array is masked with a CuPy boolean condition using where(...), the call should return a masked result and should not raise AttributeError during dtype coercion.
When a supported array backend lacks a namespace-level astype function but its array objects support astype(...), where() should still evaluate successfully.
When where() is used with NumPy-backed data or other backends that already support namespace-level astype, its observable behavior should remain unchanged.

task_16.title: Correct CombinedLock locked-state reporting
task_16.description: The upgrade fixes xarray's CombinedLock state reporting so callers can rely on CombinedLock.locked() to reflect whether any wrapped lock is actually acquired, instead of incorrectly appearing locked whenever locks are present.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `CombinedLock.locked()` reports the real lock state of a `CombinedLock`, returning locked only when at least one wrapped lock is currently acquired rather than whenever the combined lock contains lock objects.

expectation.grounded: `xarray.backends.locks.CombinedLock.locked()` should evaluate each wrapped lock by invoking its public `locked()` method and return `True` only if at least one underlying lock reports that it is locked. If none of the wrapped locks are locked, or the combined lock contains no locks, `CombinedLock.locked()` should return `False`.
expectation.conceptual: The combined lock API should accurately expose whether the combined resource is currently locked. Calling `CombinedLock.locked()` should mirror the live state of the wrapped locks rather than treating the presence of lock objects as evidence that the lock is held.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to the observable result of `CombinedLock.locked()` and must preserve the existing public API shape of `CombinedLock`. The method must continue to aggregate the state across all wrapped locks and remain compatible with lock objects that expose a callable `locked()` status method.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should not alter how callers construct or use the combined lock beyond correcting the reported lock status. Existing lock composition behavior should remain intact while the reported state becomes truthful.

behavior: `CombinedLock.locked()` now checks the runtime lock state of each wrapped lock instead of treating the `locked` attribute itself as truthy.
A `CombinedLock` with wrapped locks that are all currently unlocked reports `False` from `locked()`.
A `CombinedLock` reports `True` from `locked()` when any wrapped lock is currently locked.
A `CombinedLock` with no wrapped locks continues to report `False` from `locked()`.
acceptance_criteria: When a `CombinedLock` is created from one or more unlocked lock objects and `locked()` is called before any lock is acquired, it should return `False`.
When any underlying lock in a `CombinedLock` is acquired and `locked()` is called, it should return `True`.
When all previously acquired underlying locks are released and `locked()` is called again, it should return `False`.
When a `CombinedLock` has no wrapped locks, calling `locked()` should return `False`.

task_14.title: Extend Dataset.eval() to native N-dimensional evaluation
task_14.description: Dataset.eval() now evaluates expressions natively instead of delegating to pandas.eval(), enabling expressions and assignments on datasets with more than two dimensions while preserving array-oriented logical syntax, deprecating parser overrides, and rejecting unsupported or unsafe inputs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset.eval() can evaluate user expressions and simple assignments on datasets with more than two dimensions, while preserving array-friendly logical syntax and failing clearly for deprecated, unsupported, or unsafe usage patterns.

expectation.grounded: Dataset.eval() should accept a single expression statement or a single simple name assignment, evaluate it against dataset data variables and coordinates using xarray-native operations, and support N-dimensional array inputs rather than being limited by pandas.eval(). The evaluation namespace should expose data variables, coordinates, np, pd, xr, and a restricted set of safe builtins, with dataset variables taking precedence when names collide. Passing the parser argument should still evaluate but emit a FutureWarning because parser selection is deprecated. Boolean expressions written with and, or, not, or chained comparisons should continue to work with element-wise array semantics. Invalid syntax, unsupported statement forms, lambda expressions, private attribute access, and unavailable dangerous builtins should be rejected rather than executed.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading should be able to use Dataset.eval() for arithmetic, comparison, and assignment expressions on multidimensional datasets without hitting the previous dimensionality limit. The method should continue to accept familiar boolean expression syntax for array-wise logic, warn when callers rely on deprecated parser configuration, and reject unsupported or unsafe input instead of evaluating it.

constraints.grounded: Keep Dataset.eval() as a restricted expression interface: only one statement at a time, only one simple name on the left side of an assignment, no augmented assignment or multi-target assignment, no private attribute access, and no lambda expressions. Do not allow helper namespaces or builtins to shadow dataset data variables or coordinates during name resolution. The change should not require users to switch away from Dataset.eval() for valid expression-based workflows on higher-dimensional data.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should broaden supported array shapes without turning Dataset.eval() into arbitrary Python execution. Valid existing expression workflows should remain predictable, while malformed, unsupported, or unsafe forms should fail clearly and safely.

behavior: Dataset.eval() evaluates expressions with a native expression engine that supports datasets with more than two dimensions.
A plain expression returns the evaluated result, while a single simple assignment returns a Dataset with the computed variable added.
Leading and trailing whitespace are ignored, but the input must still be a single valid statement.
Passing the parser argument continues to work for now but emits a FutureWarning because parser selection is deprecated.

The logical keywords and, or, and not are interpreted with element-wise array semantics, and chained comparisons are interpreted as element-wise conjunctions rather than Python short-circuit comparisons.

The evaluation namespace includes dataset data variables, coordinates, np, pd, xr, and a limited safe builtin set, with dataset variables taking precedence over coordinates, helper modules, and builtins when names collide.

Invalid syntax, unsupported statement types, multiple statements, multiple assignment targets, non-name assignment targets, lambda expressions, and private attribute access are rejected with errors instead of being partially executed.
Dangerous import and file I/O builtins are not exposed inside Dataset.eval().
acceptance_criteria: When Dataset.eval() is used on a dataset whose variables have more than two dimensions, arithmetic and comparison expressions should evaluate successfully and produce the same array-wise result as the equivalent direct xarray operations.
When the statement is a single simple assignment, Dataset.eval() should return a Dataset containing the assigned variable computed from the expression.
When callers write boolean filters with and, or, not, or chained comparisons, Dataset.eval() should evaluate them using element-wise array behavior instead of failing because the operands are arrays.
When the parser argument is supplied to Dataset.eval(), the call should still evaluate but emit a FutureWarning.
When an expression references dataset variables, coordinates, helper namespaces, or safe builtins, the documented helpers should be available and dataset-defined names should win on name collisions.

When the input contains multiple statements, augmented assignment, multiple targets, non-name targets, invalid syntax, lambda expressions, private attribute access, or unavailable dangerous builtins, Dataset.eval() should fail with an error instead of executing the input.

task_17.title: Fix multi-variable GroupBy.map recombination
task_17.description: This upgrade fixes a runtime bug in xarray groupby mapping when grouping by more than one variable. Multi-variable GroupBy.map operations now recombine mapped groups safely when ordering is already contiguous, when some grouped position segments are empty, and when a grouper does not expose a current index during alignment.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that mapping over grouped datasets defined by more than one grouping variable recombines the mapped groups correctly and does not fail when some grouped combinations are empty or when grouping metadata is missing an active index for one of the groupers.

expectation.grounded: `DatasetGroupBy.map()` should support `groupby()` objects built from more than one grouping variable and return a correctly recombined result. During recombination, the operation should recognize already in-order slice-based positions as requiring no permutation, ignore empty grouped position segments when deriving output order, and align multi-grouper results to the complete grouping index even if a current grouper index is absent.
expectation.conceptual: Mapping over groups formed from multiple grouping variables should behave like a normal map operation: it should finish successfully and rebuild one correctly ordered result, including sparse group layouts where some group combinations have no members or grouping metadata is partially absent.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress existing `GroupBy.map()` behavior for unaffected cases such as single-grouping-variable inputs or already aligned outputs. Preserve observed data ordering semantics, avoid generating values for empty groups, and do not require callers to manually filter sparse multi-variable group combinations before calling `map()`.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing successful groupby-map behavior unchanged while making multi-variable grouping robust. The fix should not alter unaffected results, should not invent data for missing groups, and should not make callers restructure valid inputs to avoid the bug.

behavior: `DatasetGroupBy.map()` no longer fails solely because a multi-variable grouping result lacks a current index for one of its groupers during recombination.
When recombination positions collapse to a full in-order slice, the mapped result is treated as already ordered rather than being unnecessarily permuted.
When some grouped position segments are empty, recombination skips those empty segments instead of failing while building the final ordering.
Multi-variable mapped outputs are aligned against the full grouping index when needed so the combined result preserves the intended grouped structure.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataset is grouped by more than one variable and passed through `map()`, the call should complete successfully and return a combined dataset.
When some combinations in a multi-variable grouping contain no members, `map()` should still combine the non-empty mapped groups without error and without inventing data for the empty combinations.
When the mapped group outputs are already in final order, the recombined result should preserve that order instead of mis-ordering the data.
When recombining a multi-variable grouped result requires alignment to the full grouping index and an active grouper index is absent, the operation should still return a correctly aligned result.

task_19.title: Lock netCDF4 close operations
task_19.description: The 2026.1.0 update fixes a race condition in the netCDF4 backend by ensuring close operations participate in backend locking. File-backed, in-memory, and pre-opened netCDF4 resources should now be closed under the appropriate lock so concurrent workflows do not bypass synchronization during cleanup.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that closing xarray objects that use the netCDF4 backend is synchronized with the backend lock so concurrent cleanup does not trigger intermittent race conditions for file-backed, in-memory, or externally supplied netCDF4 datasets.

expectation.grounded: Within the netCDF4 backend, NetCDF4DataStore must propagate its lock to the manager used for filesystem paths, bytes or memoryview-backed in-memory reads, in-memory writes with a close callback, and already-open dataset handles. DummyFileManager.close() and PickleableFileManager.close() must acquire the configured lock when locking is requested, and PickleableFileManager must preserve that lock across serialization so later close operations remain synchronized.
expectation.conceptual: Any xarray workflow using the netCDF4 engine should close resources under the same synchronization used for backend access, eliminating intermittent close-time races without changing how users open or close datasets.

constraints.grounded: Do not change close behavior when no lock is configured or when locking is explicitly skipped. Preserve existing support for filesystem paths, bytes or memoryview inputs, in-memory write targets, externally supplied netCDF4 dataset objects, existing close callbacks, and the normal mode and autoclose lifecycle.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to safe synchronization during cleanup. Supported netCDF4 usage patterns, dataset contents, and the normal close lifecycle should remain otherwise unchanged.

behavior: netCDF4-backed close operations now use the configured backend lock before invoking the underlying file or dataset close path when locking is requested.
Path-backed netCDF4 datasets opened through xarray inherit close-time locking because the backend now passes the lock into the file manager used for on-disk datasets.
In-memory netCDF4 reads from bytes-like sources, in-memory writes that rely on a custom close callback, and already-open netCDF4 dataset handles also participate in close-time locking.
A PickleableFileManager retains its configured lock across serialization and deserialization so restored managers do not lose close-time synchronization.
If no lock is configured, or locking is explicitly bypassed for close, the backend continues to close resources without acquiring a lock.
acceptance_criteria: When an xarray object using the netCDF4 engine is closed after opening from a filesystem path, it should perform cleanup under the backend lock rather than using an unlocked close path.
When the netCDF4 engine is used for bytes-like in-memory reads or in-memory writes, closing should use the configured lock before closing the underlying dataset or invoking its close callback.
When xarray wraps an already-open netCDF4 dataset object, closing through xarray should be serialized by the netCDF4 backend lock.
When a locked PickleableFileManager is restored from serialized state and later closed, it should still honor the configured lock.
When no lock is configured, or close is requested without locking, close behavior should remain compatible with prior non-locking behavior.

task_18.title: CoordinateTransformIndex indexing bug fixes
task_18.description: Upgrading from 2025.12.0 to 2026.1.0 fixes CoordinateTransformIndex indexing so transform-backed coordinates behave consistently during positional and label-based selection. The update preserves expected singleton dimensions for non-scalar indexing and accepts raw NumPy label arrays during coordinate lookup.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CoordinateTransformIndex handles indexing without shape corruption: transform-backed arrays should preserve expected dimensions for outer and vectorized selections, only drop dimensions for scalar integer selections, and accept NumPy label arrays as valid coordinate labels.

expectation.grounded: CoordinateTransformIndex should treat NumPy ndarray label values passed to coordinate-based selection as sized 1D xarray label objects so size-aware alignment and multi-coordinate selection work correctly. For positional indexing, transform-backed results should no longer squeeze every singleton axis: outer indexing should preserve size-1 dimensions, while basic and vectorized indexing should squeeze only axes addressed by scalar integer indexers.
expectation.conceptual: From a user perspective, transform-backed coordinates should index like normal xarray indexes. Array-based selections should keep the shape the caller requested, scalar integer selections should still reduce rank, and plain NumPy arrays should work as coordinate labels without changing the meaning of the selection.

constraints.grounded: Keep existing validation that required transform coordinate labels must be supplied for label-based selection. Do not remove axes just because an array-based indexer or broadcasted result has length 1; only scalar integer indexers may trigger axis removal. Preserve existing coordinate-transform label resolution behavior aside from accepting raw NumPy label arrays as valid label inputs.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be non-regressive: incomplete label selections should still be rejected, singleton dimensions chosen through non-scalar indexing should remain visible, and only true scalar picks should collapse dimensions.

behavior: CoordinateTransformIndex accepts raw NumPy arrays as coordinate label inputs for label-based selection and interprets them as sized label vectors.
Coordinate-based selection can use the sizes of NumPy label arrays when resolving selections across multiple transform coordinates.
Outer or orthogonal indexing against transform-backed coordinates preserves singleton dimensions instead of squeezing every length-1 axis.
Basic and vectorized indexing still remove axes indexed by scalar integers, but they no longer remove axes selected by length-1 arrays or other non-scalar indexers.
acceptance_criteria: When a transform-backed array is indexed with array or list indexers and one selected axis has length 1, it should retain that axis with size 1 in the result.
When a transform-backed array is indexed with scalar integers, only the axes addressed by those scalar integer indexers should be removed from the result.

When sel is used with CoordinateTransformIndex and one or more coordinate labels are provided as plain NumPy arrays, the selection should succeed and use those arrays' sizes in its selection semantics.

When the same basic, outer, or vectorized selection is applied to transform-backed coordinates and to equivalent standard index-backed coordinates, the observable result shape and chosen values should match.

task_20.title: Clarify missing SciPy failures for NDPointIndex
task_20.description: The upgrade improves how the library reports a missing optional SciPy dependency for NDPointIndex. Using the SciPy-backed point index without an importable scipy installation now raises a direct, actionable ImportError instead of surfacing an indirect failure during index setup, while supported environments are expected to behave the same as before.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that using `NDPointIndex` without `scipy` installed produces a direct, actionable dependency error instead of an indirect failure during index creation.

expectation.grounded: When `NDPointIndex` is used with `ScipyKDTreeAdapter` and `scipy.spatial.KDTree` cannot be imported, initialization should raise `ImportError` immediately and make clear that `scipy` is required for this usage. When `scipy` is installed and importable, `NDPointIndex` behavior through `ScipyKDTreeAdapter` should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Users who invoke the SciPy-backed point index without the optional SciPy dependency should get a clear explanation that SciPy is required, and they should see that failure at the point where the index machinery is being created. Users with SciPy available should not experience any behavior change.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing successful `NDPointIndex` and `ScipyKDTreeAdapter` behavior when `scipy` is available. Limit the change to the missing-dependency path and keep the observable failure signal as `ImportError` tied to the SciPy requirement.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change normal point-index behavior in supported environments; only improve how unsupported environments report the missing optional dependency.

behavior: Creating the SciPy-backed tree adapter for `NDPointIndex` now intercepts failure to import SciPy's `KDTree` and raises a direct `ImportError` about the missing SciPy dependency.
The missing-dependency failure is surfaced during adapter initialization rather than appearing later as an indirect error during index creation.
In environments where `scipy` is installed and importable, the SciPy-backed `NDPointIndex` path continues to initialize and operate without intended behavioral changes.
acceptance_criteria: When a user initializes `NDPointIndex` through its SciPy-backed adapter in an environment where `scipy` is not installed or not importable, it should fail immediately with `ImportError` that clearly indicates SciPy is required.
When a user performs the same initialization in an environment where `scipy` is installed and importable, the index should initialize successfully with no new dependency-related errors.
When diagnosing a missing SciPy dependency for this feature, the surfaced error should be attributable to the `NDPointIndex` SciPy requirement rather than an unrelated downstream failure.

task_23.title: Correct rolling and coarsen window documentation
task_23.description: The 2026.1.0 update corrects misleading public documentation for rolling and coarsening window APIs by removing references to exponential windows from DataArrayRolling, DatasetRolling, and Coarsen. This change improves the accuracy of help text and generated documentation without changing runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the public rolling-window documentation accurately describes standard rolling and coarsening windows, and does not imply exponential window behavior for DataArrayRolling, DatasetRolling, or Coarsen.

expectation.grounded: The public docstrings for `DataArrayRolling`, `DatasetRolling`, and `Coarsen` should describe the `windows` mapping as creating a rolling window along a dimension, not an exponential window. Any user-visible help text or generated API documentation derived from these docstrings should reflect the corrected terminology. No runtime functionality, parameters, defaults, results, warnings, or exceptions should change in this release.
expectation.conceptual: Users reading the rolling and coarsening API documentation should see accurate terminology for the kind of window being created. The update should only fix misleading wording and should not alter how the APIs behave.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the existing public API surface and semantics of `DataArrayRolling`, `DatasetRolling`, and `Coarsen`, including accepted arguments, window sizing behavior, and current error conditions. The change must remain documentation-only and must not introduce behavioral differences in rolling or coarsening operations.
constraints.conceptual: This update must improve documentation clarity without changing results, supported usage, or observable runtime behavior for existing rolling and coarsening workflows.

behavior: User-visible documentation for `DataArrayRolling` describes the `windows` argument as defining a rolling window along the target dimension.
User-visible documentation for `DatasetRolling` describes the `windows` argument as defining a rolling window along the target dimension.
User-visible documentation for `Coarsen` describes the `windows` argument without referring to exponential window behavior.
Rolling and coarsening computations continue to behave exactly as in 2025.12.0, with no functional or API change introduced by this update.
acceptance_criteria: When a user inspects the `DataArrayRolling` documentation, it should describe a rolling window rather than an exponential window.
When a user inspects the `DatasetRolling` documentation, it should describe a rolling window rather than an exponential window.
When a user inspects the `Coarsen` documentation, it should describe the window mapping without implying exponential behavior.
When users upgrade from 2025.12.0 to 2026.1.0, rolling and coarsening operations should exhibit the same runtime behavior and public API semantics as before.

task_21.title: Clarify xarray.where attribute-handling modes
task_21.description: The `xarray.where()` API documentation now explains the supported `keep_attrs` modes and clarifies how result attributes are chosen, especially when `x` is a scalar and the default behavior does not retain attrs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can predict how `xarray.where` handles attrs across `cond`, `x`, and `y`, including the case where `x` is a scalar and the default behavior leaves the result without attrs.

expectation.grounded: Document `xarray.where(cond, x, y, keep_attrs=None)` so `keep_attrs` explicitly covers boolean aliases plus the public string modes `drop`, `identical`, `no_conflicts`, `drop_conflicts`, and `override`. The public contract should state that `override` or `True` copies attrs from `x`, `drop` or `False` returns an object with empty attrs, `identical` requires matching attrs on all contributing objects, `no_conflicts` merges attrs only when same-named attrs agree, and `drop_conflicts` merges attrs while omitting conflicting names. The documentation should also state that when `x` is a scalar, the default result has no attrs and `keep_attrs="drop_conflicts"` can preserve compatible attrs from `cond`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to read the `xarray.where` API and understand which attribute-retention modes exist, what each mode guarantees, and why metadata may disappear by default when the true branch is a scalar.

constraints.grounded: Keep the requirement limited to the documented public behavior of `xarray.where` and its `keep_attrs` parameter. Do not imply new parameters, changed return types, or unconditional preservation of attrs in scalar-input or conflicting-metadata cases.
constraints.conceptual: Clarify the existing behavior without overstating guarantees: metadata should only be retained or merged when the selected policy allows it, and conflicting metadata should not appear as preserved by default.

behavior: `xarray.where` documents `keep_attrs` as accepting boolean aliases, named merge policies, or a callable.
Using `keep_attrs=True` or `keep_attrs="override"` is documented to copy attrs from `x` onto the result without comparing attrs from other inputs.
Using `keep_attrs=False` or `keep_attrs="drop"` is documented to return a DataArray or Dataset with empty attrs.
Using `keep_attrs="identical"` is documented to require the same attrs on all participating objects.
Using `keep_attrs="no_conflicts"` is documented to merge attrs only when same-named attrs agree.
Using `keep_attrs="drop_conflicts"` is documented to merge attrs and drop names with conflicting values.
When `x` is a scalar, the documented default result has no attrs; selecting `keep_attrs="drop_conflicts"` is documented to preserve compatible attrs from `cond`.
acceptance_criteria: When a user consults the `xarray.where` API documentation, it should enumerate every supported `keep_attrs` mode and the boolean aliases.
When `xarray.where` is described with `keep_attrs=True` or `keep_attrs="override"`, it should state that result attrs come from `x`.
When `xarray.where` is described with `keep_attrs=False` or `keep_attrs="drop"`, it should state that the returned object has empty attrs.

When merge-oriented modes are described, the documentation should distinguish between matching-only behavior (`identical`), non-conflicting merge behavior (`no_conflicts`), and conflict-dropping merge behavior (`drop_conflicts`).
