When `x` is a scalar, the documentation should make clear that attrs are not retained by default and that a merge mode such as `drop_conflicts` is required to preserve compatible attrs from the condition.

task_22.title: Clarify xarray.dot coordinate alignment semantics
task_22.description: The 2026.1.0 update clarifies how xarray.dot() and DataArray.dot() interact with labeled coordinates. It makes the coordinate-alignment contract explicit so users can predict results when labels are reordered, partially overlap, or remain on dimensions that are not reduced, without introducing a runtime behavior change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the public documentation for xarray.dot() and DataArray.dot() clearly explains how coordinates affect dot-product results, including label-based alignment, the default handling of partially overlapping labels, and preservation of coordinates on dimensions that are not summed away.

expectation.grounded: The xarray.dot() and DataArray.dot() documentation should state that inputs are aligned by coordinate values rather than positional order, that the default arithmetic_join="inner" behavior includes only overlapping coordinate values in the computation, that coordinates on dimensions not reduced by the dot product remain on the result, and that xr.set_options(arithmetic_join="exact") can be used when exact coordinate matching is required.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to read the dot-product documentation and correctly predict outcomes for reordered labels, partially overlapping labels, and retained non-reduced coordinates, with clear notice that strict matching is available when silent alignment is not acceptable.

constraints.grounded: Treat this as a clarification of existing xarray.dot() and DataArray.dot() semantics rather than a new computation rule: do not imply position-based matching, non-inner joining by default, inclusion of non-overlapping labels in the calculation, or dropping coordinates from dimensions that remain after reduction.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should document the current observable contract without changing the default behavior or suggesting results that differ from label-aware alignment.

behavior: xarray.dot() aligns coordinates by coordinate value before computing the dot product, so matching is based on labels rather than the original order of values.
Under the default alignment behavior, only coordinate values shared by both inputs participate in the dot product along the reduced dimensions.
Coordinate values that do not overlap across inputs are excluded from the computation rather than being matched by position.
Coordinates attached to dimensions that are not reduced by the dot product are preserved on the output.
DataArray.dot() follows the same coordinate-alignment semantics as xarray.dot().
acceptance_criteria: When two arrays have the same coordinate labels in different orders, calling xarray.dot() should produce the result defined by matching values with the same labels before multiplication and summation.
When DataArray.dot() is used on arrays whose reduced dimension shares only some coordinate labels, it should use only the shared labels under the default behavior.
When a dot product reduces one dimension and leaves another dimension intact, the result should retain the coordinates for the dimension that remains.

When users consult the public API documentation for xarray.dot() and DataArray.dot(), they should find the coordinate-handling rules described explicitly enough to understand reordered labels, partial overlap, and preserved non-reduced coordinates.
When users need strict coordinate equality instead of default alignment, the documentation should direct them to the exact-match arithmetic_join option.

task_24.title: Clarify combine API defaults and option semantics
task_24.description: Version 2026.1.0 updates the user-facing documentation for xarray's combine helpers to explicitly state the current defaults for combine-related kwargs and to clarify how `data_vars` and `coords` behave, especially when `data_vars=None`. The change is preparatory and does not alter runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the public documentation for `combine_nested` and `combine_by_coords` clearly describes the current defaults and supported option semantics for the combine-related kwargs so users can predict how combination behaves without relying on warnings or source inspection.

expectation.grounded: The API documentation for `combine_nested` and `combine_by_coords` should explicitly list `compat='no_conflicts'`, `data_vars='all'`, `coords='different'`, and `join='outer'` as the defaults. It should document that `data_vars` accepts `None` as well as string modes and lists of variable names, and that `data_vars=None` resolves to `'all'` when `concat_dim` is absent from all input objects and to `'minimal'` when `concat_dim` is present in any input object. It should also describe the `coords` modes directly, including the behavior of `'minimal'`, `'different'`, `'all'`, and explicit coordinate-name lists.
expectation.conceptual: Users reading the combine API docs should see the actual default settings and a clear explanation of how variable and coordinate selection works during combination, including the special meaning of `data_vars=None`.

constraints.grounded: This upgrade must not change the runtime behavior, default execution path, or result semantics of `combine_nested` or `combine_by_coords`; it only clarifies the documented contract for existing public kwargs and their accepted values.
constraints.conceptual: The release should improve clarity without changing how combine operations behave in running code.

behavior: The user-facing docs for `combine_nested` now surface the default values for `compat`, `data_vars`, `coords`, and `join` instead of leaving them implicit.
The user-facing docs for `combine_by_coords` now surface the same default values and describe the `coords` options directly rather than only cross-referencing `data_vars`.
The documented type and option contract for `data_vars` in both APIs now explicitly includes `None` and list-of-string inputs.

The documented meaning of `data_vars=None` now states that it behaves like `'all'` when `concat_dim` is not present in any input object and like `'minimal'` when `concat_dim` is present in at least one input object.

The documented coordinate-selection contract now distinguishes `'minimal'`, `'different'`, `'all'`, and explicit coordinate-name lists, including that `'different'` may require loading coordinate payloads to compare them.
acceptance_criteria: When a user consults the API reference for `combine_nested`, it should show explicit defaults for `compat`, `data_vars`, `coords`, and `join`.
When a user consults the API reference for `combine_by_coords`, it should show the same explicit defaults and describe each `coords` mode in place.
When a user reads either API's `data_vars` documentation, it should state that `None` is accepted and explain when it behaves like `'all'` versus `'minimal'`.

When a user reads either API's parameter documentation, list-valued `data_vars` and `coords` inputs should be described as lists of variable or coordinate names rather than ambiguous internal terminology.
Upgrading to 2026.1.0 should not change the observed runtime behavior of combine operations; the improvement is limited to clearer public documentation.

task_26.title: Optimize CFMaskCoder decode copying
task_26.description: The CF mask decoding path now performs masking on a single copied output array instead of sometimes creating an additional array during decode. This reduces memory overhead and stabilizes copy behavior while preserving decoded values.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CF mask decoding produces the same masked output while reducing unnecessary array copying during decoding.

expectation.grounded: The decode path used by xarray.coding.variables.CFMaskCoder should return a newly materialized array in the requested dtype, replace every configured encoded fill value with the decoded fill value in that returned array, and avoid the extra result allocation that previously occurred in some masking cases.
expectation.conceptual: Decoding CF-masked data should preserve the decoded values users expect while using less memory and more predictable copying behavior, especially for large arrays.

constraints.grounded: The optimization must not change which values are treated as fill values, must continue honoring dtype conversion on the returned data, and must not mutate the caller's original input array during decoding.
constraints.conceptual: The performance improvement must not alter the decoded content, type handling, or the expectation that decoding operates on an independent result rather than modifying the source data.

behavior: CF mask decoding now starts from a copied output array, so the returned array is always a distinct materialized result.
When one or more encoded fill values are defined, every element matching any of those values is replaced with the decoded fill value in the returned array.
When no encoded fill values are defined, decoding returns the copied data unchanged instead of performing masking work.
The masking step no longer requires allocating a second post-mask array, so the decode path consistently performs a single copy.
acceptance_criteria: When CFMaskCoder decodes data with encoded fill values, it should return data where all matching encoded fill values are replaced by the decoded fill value.
When CFMaskCoder decodes data without any encoded fill values, it should return the same values in a new array of the requested dtype without additional masking effects.
When decoding runs on input that already matches the target dtype or requires dtype conversion, it should still produce a separate decoded array without mutating the original input.
When decoding large masked arrays, it should avoid the previous extra array allocation and complete the masking step using a single materialized output copy.

task_25.title: Fast-path explicit standard xarray engines
task_25.description: This upgrade reduces cold-start overhead when opening datasets with an explicit built-in xarray engine by bypassing full backend plugin discovery for standard engines. It preserves normal discovery for external engines and changes known-engine dependency failures to surface as backend import errors instead of unknown-engine errors.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that explicitly selecting a standard xarray engine when opening a dataset avoids first-call backend plugin discovery overhead, while preserving normal plugin lookup for non-standard engines and surfacing missing optional dependencies for known engines as dependency/import failures rather than unknown-engine failures.

expectation.grounded: When `xarray.open_dataset(..., engine=<engine_name>)` is given a built-in engine string, backend selection should resolve that backend directly instead of enumerating installed engines first. Built-in engines should still initialize normally, and if a known built-in engine cannot be imported because its optional dependency is unavailable, the call should surface the backend's `ImportError`. Engine strings that are not built-in should continue through normal engine discovery, and truly unrecognized engine names should still raise `ValueError`. Passing a backend entrypoint class directly should remain supported.
expectation.conceptual: Passing a known built-in engine by name should make dataset opening start quickly even on the first call, without changing which backend is used. Users should get a clear missing-dependency/import failure when they request a known engine that is unavailable, while third-party engines and unknown names should continue to follow the existing discovery and validation behavior.

constraints.grounded: Apply the fast path only to standard built-in engine names supplied as strings. Do not remove or weaken plugin discovery for third-party engines, do not accept unknown engine names silently, and do not regress support for backend classes passed directly instead of strings.
constraints.conceptual: Optimize only the common built-in-engine path. Existing extensibility for external backends must continue to work, unsupported engine names must still be rejected, and alternate explicit backend selection forms must keep working as before.

behavior: Explicit built-in engine names are resolved without first loading the full installed-backend registry, reducing cold-start latency for dataset opening.
Known built-in engines continue to select their normal backend implementation when requested by name.
Requesting a known built-in engine whose optional dependency is missing now surfaces the backend's import-related failure instead of reporting the engine name as unrecognized.
Non-built-in engine names still use the existing plugin discovery path, and unknown engine names continue to fail as unrecognized.
acceptance_criteria: When a process calls `xarray.open_dataset` with an explicit built-in engine name for the first time, it should avoid the startup penalty caused by full backend plugin discovery.
When a caller requests a supported built-in engine by name, it should resolve to that backend and proceed with normal dataset opening behavior.

When a caller requests a known built-in engine but the required optional package for that engine is not importable, the operation should fail with an import/dependency error for that engine rather than an unknown-engine error.
When a caller requests a third-party engine by name, backend resolution should continue to use the normal discovery path.
When a caller passes an unknown engine name, the operation should still reject it as an unrecognized engine.

task_27.title: Document Pixi Version Guidance for Contributors
task_27.description: The update adds contributor-facing guidance about the Pixi version expected for project setup and contribution workflows. The change is intended to reduce confusion from tool-version mismatches and does not change library runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the contribution guidance clearly states the relevant Pixi version expectation needed for contributor setup and workflow use.

expectation.grounded: Contributor-facing documentation should include a note about the Pixi version to use or support when following the project's contributing instructions. The release evidence indicates a documentation update only, with no corresponding public runtime API or behavioral change in the provided code diff.
expectation.conceptual: People contributing to the project should be told which Pixi version line is expected so the documented setup process is unambiguous and less likely to fail because of an incompatible tool version.

constraints.grounded: This change should remain limited to documentation for contributor workflow expectations around Pixi version usage. It should not introduce changes to runtime behavior, Python APIs, data handling, warnings, exceptions, or other library-facing semantics.
constraints.conceptual: The release should only clarify contributor setup guidance and must not change how the library behaves for end users.

behavior: Contributor documentation surfaces a Pixi version note as part of the contributing guidance.
The upgrade does not introduce any observable runtime or public API behavior change in the library.
acceptance_criteria: When a developer reads the contributing guidance after upgrading, they should find an explicit note describing the expected or supported Pixi version for that workflow.
When upgrading from 2025.12.0 to 2026.1.0, library runtime behavior and public API usage should remain unchanged by this release item.
